# The visual editor

The visual editor lets you make a game without typing code: **draw** sprites, **place** them on the screen and describe
what happens with **rules**. The editor writes an ordinary QRG program for you (open the *Code* tab to read it, or press
*Open in code editor* to keep working by hand — the link back is one way).

## The four tabs

* **Objects** — object *types* (a picture, a color and a size), drawn on an 8 × 8 grid or picked from the sprite library.
  Tap *Place on the screen* and tap the stage to put objects there; tap an object to select it and drag to move it.
* **Rules** — what the game does. Each rule reads like a sentence: **WHEN** something happens, **IF** conditions hold, **DO** actions.
* **Game** — background color, **variables** (numbers such as *score* and *lives*, optionally shown on the screen) and project tools.
* **Code** — the generated program, with its QR size.

Press **▶ Test** to play the game right under the stage while you edit; everything is saved automatically on your device.

## Writing rules

Rules run from top to bottom, every frame. *Objects touch* and *reaches an edge* give the actions two helpers:
**this object** and **the other object**. A field that takes a number accepts a plain number *or any JavaScript expression*:
`120`, `R(200)` (random), `a.x + 4` (this object's x), `score * 2`, `-Math.abs(b.vy)`.
Text can contain `{variable}` placeholders, e.g. `SCORE {score}`.

Inside rules that have them, `a` is *this object* and `b` is *the other object*; objects have the fields `x y vx vy w h c`.

### WHEN (triggers)

| Name | Sentence |
|---|---|
| Game starts | the game starts |
| Every frame | every frame |
| Button pressed | button *btn* is pressed |
| Button held | button *btn* is held down |
| Finger on screen | a finger is on the screen |
| Screen tapped | the screen is tapped |
| Object tapped | *a* is tapped |
| Objects touch | *a* touches *b* |
| Reaches an edge | *a* reaches *edge* |
| Every N seconds | every *n* seconds |

### IF (conditions)

| Name | Sentence |
|---|---|
| Variable compare | *v* *op* *n* |
| Number of objects | number of *k* *op* *n* |
| Random chance | *n*% chance |
| Button held | button *btn* is held |
| Position | *w* *axis* *op* *n* |
| JavaScript test | JavaScript is true: *js* |

### DO (actions)

| Name | Sentence |
|---|---|
| Move | move *w* by x *dx* y *dy* |
| Put at | put *w* at x *x* y *y* |
| Follow the finger | move *w* to the finger (*axis*) |
| Set speed | set the speed of *w* to x *dx* y *dy* |
| Speed up | speed up *w* by x *dx* y *dy* |
| Bounce | bounce *w* *axis* |
| Keep on screen | keep *w* on the screen |
| Destroy | destroy *w* |
| Change color | change the color of *w* to *c* |
| Create object | create *k* at x *x* y *y* with speed x *vx* y *vy* |
| Change a variable | *v* *vop* *n* |
| Play sound | play a sound at *n* Hz |
| Show text | show the text *s* at x *x* y *y* in *c* |
| End the game | end the game and show *s* |
| Restart | restart the game |
| Run JavaScript | run JavaScript: *js* |

## Starter projects

* **Coin catcher** — Drag to catch coins and dodge skulls.
* **Bouncing ball** — Keep the ball in play with the paddle.
* **Tap the targets** — Tap targets before the screen fills up.

Open *Game → Project* to start from one of them.

## Using code and rules together

* **Run JavaScript** (an action) and **JavaScript test** (a condition) let you drop a line of code into any rule.
* The generated program uses the same library as hand-written games (`kind`, `add`, `touch`, `each`, `step`, `draw`…), so it is
  a good way to learn the language: make something visually, then read the *Code* tab.
